text.p: - Russia is considering stepping up military aid to Tajikistan in the wake of the Taleban militia's onslaught in neighbouring Afghanistan.
- Russian negotiators, fresh from an annual IMF meeting in Washington, return to Moscow confident and satisfied.
- Russian agrarians stake claim to a huge part of the 1997 budget, predicting the industry will collapse unless it is propped up by enormous state subsidies.
- Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov throws down the gauntlet to security chief Alexander Lebed over his performance in rebel Chechnya.
- President Boris Yeltsin finishes his administration reshuffle.
- Security chief Lebed is put through the shredder by Interior Minister Kulikov at Wednesday's parliament session over peace accords on Chechnya.
- Russia is to tighten its grip on alcohol producers and traders.
- Chechen rebel leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev is coming to Moscow to try to get money from the state budget for his separatist republic.
